deviations.summary: Two HTTP 200 Imperva/Incapsula challenge pages were classified as valid permissive robots files, and six requests were authorised on that basis
deviations.detail: fetchRobotsPolicy decided the disposition from the status code alone, so www.nzsis.govt.nz/robots.txt and www.protectivesecurity.govt.nz/robots.txt - each HTTP 200, content-type text/html, 212 bytes, sha256 d02032286070b4dd, an Incapsula challenge document - were recorded as disposition 'rules'. parseRobots finds no directives in HTML and returns no groups, so isAllowed answered 'no applicable rule' and the log asserted that robots permitted /user/register on the evidence of a document that is not a robots file. RFC 9309 section 2.3 requires a UTF-8 text/plain representation. Six permits were issued under that reading and all six requests were made; every one returned a challenge page and none returned agency content, so no candidate evidence was obtained and no candidate set rests on any of them. The incorrect checks r-0012 and r-0013 are retained unchanged, because a permit must point at the evidence that existed when it was issued; the corrected re-reads under selection-v1.0.21 are r-0015 and r-0016, which classify the byte-identical responses as unestablished. The records of the six requests were written approximately 81 minutes after the navigations, which permitAudit discloses as recordedLate.

deviations.summary: d-0245's note claims the ECART site publishes no application form; later rendered evidence does not support a claim that broad, and it is narrowed here to what bounded discovery established
deviations.detail: d-0245 (sitemap, ecart.health.govt.nz, service-application v1, outcome no-candidates) carries the note 'a SilverStripe sitemap index; this committee site publishes no application form'. The second clause is a claim about what the site publishes, which that sitemap retrieval did not establish. Later rendered evidence bears on it: render g-0055 (sha256 856bf12907119699, 17900 bytes, headless) of https://ecart.health.govt.nz/footer/contact-us/, introduced by d-0267 and judged by d-0439, exposes a link 'Application forms' to https://ecart.health.govt.nz/publications-and-resources/application-forms/ - a directory index. That index was NOT opened and no new round was started, because Amendment 8 fixes that a link to a home page or a directory index is not a direct link to a form and that discovery does not crawl outward from one; following it after the held-out evidence had been read would expand the frozen method. The defensible conclusion is therefore only that bounded discovery found no directly linked application form for ECART in the service-application category - not that the site publishes none. Scope of this correction: nothing else changes. d-0245 is preserved unchanged and remains outcome no-candidates; d-0267 and d-0439 remain no-candidates for enquiry-or-contact (the rendered contact page carries no control at all); the Ministry of Health service-application v1 approved set is unchanged at its four PDFs; no candidate set, agency resolution or selected page is affected; and no request was made for this disclosure.

deviations.summary: Four approved Ministry of Health sitemap records claim what a child sitemap lists, and no child sitemap was ever retrieved
deviations.detail: d-0276, d-0278, d-0280 and d-0282 each state that the index's "SiteTree sitemap lists /footer/contact-us/, inspected separately". The log contains NO retrieval of any child sitemap: zero of its 464 permits were ever issued for a child-sitemap URL, and no record of any kind carries such a URL. The clause asserting what the child sitemap LISTS therefore rests on no recorded retrieval. The log cannot settle which of two things happened, and both are reportable: either a child sitemap was requested without a permit and without a record, which would be unrecorded traffic, or the claim was inferred from the construct and from the page being independently known, then written as though it had been read. The second is the more likely reading, because /footer/contact-us/ on all four origins had just been inspected directly under permits p-0058 to p-0061 as records d-0265 to d-0268, so its existence needed no sitemap to establish, and because the same agency's other index notes, such as d-0245, claim only that the document is an index and make no claim about its children. What survives in each record is the supported part: the resource retrieved was a SilverStripe sitemap index, and /footer/contact-us/ was inspected separately and directly. The clause about what the child sitemap lists is withdrawn. The four records are preserved unedited and this deviation is the disclosure. No page was requested for this record.

deviations.summary: d-0971 claims the SIA sitemaps were served unlike every previous agency in this study, which is false
deviations.detail: d-0971, the Social Investment Agency robots record, states that /sitemap.xml was a conventional guess at both origins and that "unlike every previous agency in this study it was SERVED at both, returning a sitemapindex". The second clause is false. The log holds 61 served sitemap records, 44 of whose notes describe an index: SilverStripe sitemap indexes were served and recorded no-candidates at the Ministry of Health from d-0159 onwards, and at the New Zealand Defence Force from d-0447, d-0467 through d-0472 and again at d-0528 through d-0536. The claim is withdrawn. What survives is the supported part: both SIA origins publish the same 59-byte policy, byte for byte, recorded as r-0083 and r-0084 and refreshed for this round; the whole policy is User-agent: * with Disallow: /*/allchanges and Disallow: /*/changes, which are SilverStripe page-history views and bear on nothing in this category; nothing restricts /Security/login or either search path; and no Sitemap directive is declared, so /sitemap.xml was indeed a conventional guess at both origins. This deviation is the correction mechanism because d-0971 carries no render, so correct-discovery cannot reach it, and superseding it through discovery would consume a permit and so assert a robots request that must not be made again. That is the same reasoning under which v-0002 narrowed d-0245's overbroad note rather than editing it. The record is preserved unedited. No page was requested for this record.

deviations.summary: A robots request was made to document reuse, breaching the explicit no-refetch instruction, and d-0987 claims the opposite
deviations.detail: The Social Investment Agency service-application round was instructed to use the existing fresh robots policies with no refetch. The policies authorising the round WERE reused: r-0083 and r-0084, fetched at 2026-10-02T21:08Z, were inside the 24-hour window and every permit in the round rests on them, including the preflight for the robots record itself, which reported them as reused. But a separate robots request nevertheless occurred, solely to create the round's robots DISCOVERY record: permit p-0477 authorised https://www.sia.govt.nz/robots.txt, f-0005 retrieved it at 2026-10-03T08:04:13Z, and d-0987 records that retrieval. The response was 59 bytes with the same digest as the cached policy, d193ff18, so no permission and no outcome changed, and the traffic is fully accounted for by its permit and retained bytes. It was still a request that should not have been made. d-0987's note says the procedure REUSED the policies "rather than refetching", which is false of the record carrying it: that clause described the authorisation correctly and the record's own provenance incorrectly, and it is withdrawn. What survives is the rest of the note: both origins publish the same 59-byte policy, the two patterns disallowed are SilverStripe page-history views bearing on nothing in this category, nothing restricts either search path, and no Sitemap directive is declared. The cause is structural rather than careless. The robots method's discovery record can only be created by , which requires a permit, and a permit asserts a request - so documenting reuse required making a request. The repair is a no-network policy-reuse record path, which carries no permit and no navigation timestamp and cites a fresh recorded robots check instead; until that exists, this round's record is the honest account of what happened. No corrective request is made for this deviation.

deviations.summary: v-0005 lost a word to shell substitution and reads: created by , which requires a permit
deviations.detail: v-0005 explains why the robots refetch happened structurally, and one sentence lost a word when it was recorded. It reads "The robots method... discovery record can only be created by , which requires a permit". The missing word is the name of the command: the discovery recorder. It was eaten by shell command substitution, because the word was wrapped in backticks in the text passed to the CLI and the shell evaluated it instead of passing it through. The sentence should read: the robots method... discovery record can only be created by the discovery command, which requires a permit, and a permit asserts a request - so documenting reuse required making a request. Nothing else in v-0005 is affected and its substance is unchanged: the policies authorising the round were reused, a separate robots request nevertheless occurred under p-0477 and f-0005 to create d-0987, it changed no permission or outcome, and the "rather than refetching" clause in d-0987 is withdrawn. Deviations are append-only and carry no supersession field, so this is recorded as its own entry rather than by editing v-0005. No page was requested for this record.

candidateSets.approvalNote: Re-approved after re-binding. The set now stands on d-0309 rather than the superseded d-0301: d-0309 is the rendered-DOM judgement of no-candidates for account-registration, citing render g-0001 from d-0306. Zero candidates, under a discovery round that was withheld on two of three origins because both serve Imperva/Incapsula challenges in place of robots.txt. This does not mean NZSIS publishes no registration form. See v-0001 and Amendment 30.

One candidate: the NZSIS national-security reporting form at providinginformation.nzsis.govt.nz, identified from render g-0001 (efe26268, 15971 bytes, re-verified). Discovery on the other two origins was withheld, not performed: both serve Imperva/Incapsula challenges in place of robots.txt, so no policy could be established and no request was made. Approving this set means this one URL is what should be assessed, not that it is eligible.

Approved under selection-v1.0.37, whose unjudged-render gate this set passed at approval: all 16 rendered observations in the round carry exactly one matching judgement for their own category and round. Five candidates locked from 50 active records across 10 websites. Exact sign-in URLs and the category-specific /cadet-join.html are included; portal roots and the how-do-i-join landing pages are excluded under Amendment 8, and the three event-registration forms are excluded because registering for an event is not registering an account. The shared SmartProcure URL is deduplicated across the two nzdf.mil.nz websites. wp-login.php sorts sixth and falls beyond the frozen bound of five; it is not assessed. Eight active records yielded no candidate judgement: robots-unestablished x2 (Veterans' Affairs, an Imperva challenge in place of robots.txt, withheld without any content request) and retrieval-blocked x6 (Air Force Museum reCAPTCHA in both browser modes, CadetNet Cloudflare 403 headless before a successful headed read, and the CadetNet sitemap). Approving this set means these five URLs are what should be assessed, not that any is eligible.

Approved. Two candidates from 66 active records across ten websites: https://www.defencecareers.mil.nz/apply, reached from "Apply Now" on the Defence Careers home page (g-0087), and https://www.cadetnet.org.nz/2025/08/11/applications-2025_international_sea_cadet_exchanges/, a dated post announcing applications that only the internal search reached (g-0112, g-0114, g-0116). Both are admitted on path and title alone under Amendment 8 as specific content pages rather than home pages or directory indexes; neither was opened during discovery, so nothing yet establishes that either carries a form. Thirteen active records yielded no candidate judgement: robots-unestablished x2 (Veterans' Affairs, an Imperva challenge in place of robots.txt, withheld with no content request) and retrieval-blocked x11 (the Air Force Museum searches and the CadetNet headless attempts and sitemap, all Cloudflare or reCAPTCHA, several with headed fallbacks recorded). Defence Careers' internal search was disallowed for three terms by the "*" group and recorded without being requested. Approving this set means these two URLs are what should be assessed, not that either is eligible.

Approved. Five candidates from 64 active records across ten websites, exactly at the frozen bound of five with none dropped. Every one carries a name-collecting control on the page as rendered rather than behind a link: the Defence Careers contact form (FirstName, Surname, Email, Enquiry, Message, reCAPTCHA) and the four museum and cadet-forces contact forms. Thirteen active records yielded no candidate judgement: robots-unestablished x2, Veterans' Affairs withheld for a third round under its Imperva challenge with no content request, and retrieval-blocked x11, chiefly the Air Force Museum searches and the CadetNet headless attempts. Defence Careers' internal search was disallowed for all three terms and recorded without being requested. CadetNet's emergency-contacts and cadet-school-contact-list pages were not admitted: both are directories of contact details rather than direct links to a form. Approving this set means these five URLs are what should be assessed, not that any is eligible.

Approved. Four candidates in canonical order from 63 active records across 12 websites, using all four discovery methods, within the frozen bound of five. Twelve frame-origin robots policies were refreshed because the earlier checks had crossed 24 hours, and all twelve are byte-identical to the previous observation with no disposition changed; servewise.alcohol.org.nz's policy was ESTABLISHED FOR THE FIRST TIME, returning 404 and therefore allow-all, and no content request has been made to it. Stated disallows were honoured without requesting the paths: www.healthnz.govt.nz publishes Disallow: / and was not requested in any category, which matters because it is the largest website in this agency's frame; Safer Gambling and Smokefree disallow /search, their own search form's action, closing the internal-search method on those two websites by policy, and also /user/register; HealthEd and the resource store disallow /account. Sixteen active records in THIS ROUND yielded no candidate judgement, all retrieval-blocked, from five origins that refuse non-browser fetches with HTTP 403 on robots, sitemap and content alike, two of them refusing headed Chromium as well. Two of the four candidates are already known to be unreachable by the frozen method and are admitted deliberately so the log shows registration forms were located rather than absent: /account/register is closed by stated policy, and my.health.nz's sign-up is a client-side dialog with no addressable URL. Approving this set means these four URLs are what should be assessed, not that any is eligible.

supersededCandidateSets.approvalNote: Discovery filtered four published DOCX application forms out of the candidate set instead of recording them as candidates and excluding them under criterion five. A nil set conflates 'no form found' with 'forms found, all ineligible', which are different findings; the exclude stage exists to keep them apart. The note on the workforce-survey record also gave the wrong reason: criterion two requires a form to be REACHED FROM a frame website, not hosted on one, and a directly linked third-party form is explicitly in scope.
supersededCandidateSets.supersededReason: Redo with document application forms recorded as candidates and excluded under criterion five, and with the survey's category mismatch recorded as the reason rather than its host.

supersededCandidateSets.approvalNote: The round-1 discovery note on the Māori Development Fund page was inaccurate: it stated that applications are eight PDFs excluded by criterion five. supersededCandidateSets.approvalNote: Round 2's two NOT NAVIGATED internal-search records carry navigatedAt timestamps and were counted in the five-second navigation pacing, so the raw data asserts a navigation the notes deny.
